subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Should shared auth-profile OAuth refresh retry ordinary transient provider and network failures, and which error classes and total time budget are permitted?
rationale: The current provider interface has no generic retryability contract, and retrying the wrong OAuth error can replay terminal or rotating-token requests while holding the shared refresh lock.

options.title: Shared classified retry
options.body: Retry only explicitly transient network, timeout, rate-limit, and retryable HTTP failures within the existing lock and one bounded overall deadline.

options.title: Provider-owned retry
options.body: Extend provider and plugin refresh contracts so each owner defines and executes its own retry classification and budget.

options.title: Keep single-shot behavior
options.body: Retain the current immediate failure behavior and rely on existing adoption, fallback, cooldown, restart, or reauthentication paths.

recommendation.title: Shared classified retry
recommendation.body: Retry only explicitly transient network, timeout, rate-limit, and retryable HTTP failures within the existing lock and one bounded overall deadline.

likelyOwner.reason: The central OAuth lifecycle manager and adjacent hardening history make Vincent Koc the strongest individual routing candidate, with secops review still appropriate.
